1 THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 01.08.2024.2024, THE COURT ON 04.10.2024 DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2 MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502  JUDGMENT

The petitioners in O.P.(MV)No.715 of 2017 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Muvattupuzha (hereinafter referred to as "MACT") have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 05.07.2019 issued by the MACT.
2. The short facts necessary for the disposal of this appeal are as follows:
The 2nd appellant herein and Smt.Bhavaniamma, the mother of the appellants were travelling in a car bearing registration No.KL- 44-A-5154 along the Muvattupuzha - Kothamangalam road.
When they reached Mathirappilly, the car in which they were travelling collided with another car bearing registration No.KL-36-E-6007 which was coming from the opposite direction.
The 2 nd appellant and Smt.Bhavaniamma sustained severe injuries and they were hospitalised at Medical College Hospital, Kolencherry.
Smt.Bhavaniamma was treated as an inpatient from 28.05.2017 to 04.07.2017.
She was discharged also on 04.07.2017 and was staying in her residence thereafter.
However, on 14.07.2017, MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 Smt.Bhavaniamma passed away, allegedly on account of the injuries sustained by her at the time of the accident on 28.05.2017.

3. In such circumstances, O.P.(MV) No.715 of 2017 was filed before the MACT, by the appellants herein contending that the accident is the result of rash and negligent driving of the car bearing registration No.KL-44-A-5154 by the 1st respondent in the claim petition.
The 2nd respondent in the claim petition was the owner of the car concerned and the 3rd respondent before the Tribunal was the insurer.
4. Respondents 1 and 2 before the MACT - the driver and the owner of the vehicle chose to remain ex parte.

The 3rd respondent before the MACT - the 1st respondent herein filed a written statement denying the age, occupation and income of the deceased, also contending that the death of Smt.Bhavaniamma had no proximity to the road traffic accident since the deceased was discharged on 04.07.2017 whereas the death took place only on 14.07.2017.

5. The Tribunal by the impugned award dated 05.07.2019 found that the accident occurred on account of the negligence on MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 the part of the driver of the vehicle - 1st respondent before the Tribunal.

However, as regards the 2nd question "whether the Saraswathy.K.K vs The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152309315/
2 death of the deceased is due to the injuries sustained in the accident?", the Tribunal found as under:
"Issue No.2 in O.P.No.715/2017:- According to the petitioners the deceased died due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

sentences.text: According to the 3rd respondent, on the other hand, the death has no connection with the injuries sustained in the accident.
A perusal of Ext.A12 post-mortem report shows that the death is due to myocardial infraction.
Ext.A11 is the discharge summary.
It shows that she was discharged with advice of suture removal at a local hospital next Tuesday.
According to the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent, this will show that the deceased was discharged since she recovered from the injuries sustained in the accident.
According to the learned counsel A11 and A12 would show that death of the deceased has absolutely no connection with the injuries sustained in the accident.
10. In this context it is worth referring to the evidence tendered by PW2.
PW2 is the professor Neurosurgery MOSC Medical College Hospital, Kolenchery who examined the deceased.
He would also say that Ext.A11 was issued from his hospital.

According to PW2 any patient, especially old aged person with polytrauma and who have undergone multiple surgeries and nonambulent have high risk of myocardiac MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 infraction.
Admittedly, the deceased was aged 80.
The evidence tendered by PW2 also do not show that the injuries sustained in the accident have anything to do with the death of Bhavaniamma.
Ext.A11 shows that the petitioner was symptomatically better and hence discharged with an advise of removal of stitches.
As it stands now there is absolutely nothing to show that the death of the deceased is due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Therefore, the issue is answered accordingly."
Thus, the Tribunal found that the death of the deceased cannot be related to the injuries sustained in the accident.

Ultimately, by the impugned award, the learned Tribunal refused the claim as against:
i. Funeral expenses - Rs.50,000/-
ii. Loss of dependency- Rs.10,00,000/-
iii. Love and affection- Rs.1,00,000/-
iv. Loss of estate - Rs. 2,00,000/-

At the same time, awarding certain reduced amounts on the claim against transport to the hospital,
damage to clothing and articles, expenses for nursing and attending, pain and suffering etc.
As against the total claim limited to Rs.7,00,000/-, Rs.2,53,462/- was ultimately awarded by the MACT.

sentences.text: 3 6. It is challenging the above award that the captioned appeal is filed by the appellants herein.
7. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants and the learned counsel appearing for the respondent herein.

8. The main issue arising for consideration in this appeal is as to the legality or otherwise of the findings of the MACT to the effect that the death of the deceased cannot be attributed to the injuries sustained in the accident.
It is true that the accident occurred on 28.05.2017 and the deceased was hospitalised only from 28.05.2017 to 04.07.2017, on which date she was discharged.
It is also true that the death has taken place after 10 days of the discharge, on 14.07.2017.
A perusal of the wound certificate - Annexure A10, shows that the deceased had sustained serious injuries on account of the accident.
She had an open fracture on the middle of left Tibia as well as a contusion on the left side of the chest.
Similarly, there was a fracture on the right Tibia and right Fibula.
There was also a depressed fracture on the right frontal bone also.
The deceased was hospitalised from 28.05.2017 till MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 04.07.2017, for 37 days.
The discharge summary - Annexure A11, shows that while in the hospital, the deceased had to undergo a serious surgery on 07.06.2017.
Post the said operation, the discharge summary points out, that the deceased developed "wound gaping" and she had to undergo a secondary closure.
Thus, the fact that the petitioner had suffered serious injuries like compound fractures and that she had undergone a major surgery is not in dispute.
The post-mortem certificate at Annexure A12, on the other hand, opines that the cause of death is due to "myocardial infarction".
The very same post-mortem certificate notices that there was a healing wound on the left leg behind the knee and the right knee was in a cast.
It is also noticed that the deceased was having bed sore in the lower back.

The Tribunal, in paragraph 10 of its award, appears to have placed much reliance on the evidence tendered by PW2 to arrive at the conclusion that injuries sustained in the accident have nothing to do with the death of the deceased.

At the same time, I have perused the evidence of PW2, wherein he has specifically pointed out that "any patient, especially old-aged person, with polytrauma and who have undergone multiple MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 surgeries and non-ambulant, have a high risk of myocardial infarction".
Therefore, the evidence of PW2 appears to be the other way around.
PW2 doctor has stated in evidence that any patient, leave alone old age patients with polytrauma and who have undergone multiple surgeries have a high risk of myocardial infarction.
The deceased admittedly had undergone multiple surgeries and was also facing accident trauma.
In such circumstances, the findings of the Tribunal in paragraph 10 referred to above does not appear to be the correct legal position.
9. In Vidhyawati v. A. Guruswamy [2005 ACJ 433], the Calcutta High Court was called upon to consider an almost similar issue.

Considering the above question, the Calcutta High Court has held as under:
"It is now settled position of law that if the cause of death is integrally connected with the injury sustained in the accident and is one in the chain of causa causens, the cause of death must be attributed to the injury suffered in the accident."

4 10.

A Division Bench of this Court in Venugopal v. Paulson [2008 (4) KLT 920], considered the claim made by the legal representatives of the deceased who committed suicide due to MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 mental depression developed consequent to the injuries sustained by the deceased in an accident.

The findings rendered by this Court are as under:
"4.
In this case, it has been in evidence that before the accident, the deceased had no depression.
There is no evidence to the effect that the deceased has suffered depression leading to suicide or any other psychological disorder before the accident.
He was a happy family man before the dreadful accident.
The Doctor also deposed that before the accident no such depression was reported.
From the evidence, it can be seen that his severe depression and worthilessness and helplessness came after the accident in view of the accidental injuries.
In his severe depressed state, he felt that he was a greater burden to his relative's life.
Suicide was his decision and worthilessness and helplessness which were the result of his depression which, in turn, resulted in the suicide.

Therefore, we are of the view that compensation should be given to the legal representative for the death as death was caused due to the mental depression developed consequent to the injuries, but, we are of the opinion that on the facts and circumstances of this case, a reduction can be given and only 50% of the compensation payable for the death need be granted."

Thus, it is clear that, even in a case where the death has occurred on account of suicide, a claim petition made by legal representatives MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 has to be considered, with respect to the question as to whether the suicide can be attributed to the accident that has occurred.

11. This Court also notices the judgment of another Division Bench of this Court in State of Kerala v.
Narayanankutty [1980 KLT 908], wherein the death pursuant to head injury after eleven days arose for consideration with reference to the provisions of the Indian Penal Code.

Considering the above issue, this Court at paragraph 14 has found as under:
"14.
An injury may lead to death.
Death may be instantaneous or may be delayed.

The injury may lead to shock, excessive bleeding, coma, syncope etc. and cause death; in such a case injury and death have a clearly perceptible and direct nexus and there will be no difficulty in finding that death is the direct result of injury.

The decision may not be so easy in a case where death is caused not directly by the injury itself but due to a complication or development or in a case where death is not instantaneous but is delayed.
Where death is delayed or due to later complication or development, court has to consider the nature of the injury, complication or development and attendant circumstances.

If the complication or development is the natural or probable or necessary consequence of the injury and if it is reasonably contemplated as its result,
the injury can be said to have caused death.

If, on the other hand, the chain of consequences is broken or if there is unexpected MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 complication causing new mischief, the relation of cause and effect is not established or the causal connection is too remote and the injury cannot be said Saraswathy.K.K vs The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152309315/
5 to have caused death.

sentences.text: If the original injury itself is of a fatal nature, it makes no difference that death is actually caused by a complication naturally flowing from the injury and not the injury itself, since causal connection is proximate."
The principles laid down in the above judgment, have a bearing on the facts and circumstances of the case at hand also.

Here also, though, the death of the deceased was on 14.07.2017, after her discharge on 04.07.2017, the fact that the deceased had to undergo serious surgery pursuant to the accident is not in dispute.
The evidence of the doctor-PW2, also supports the above conclusion.
12. As noticed earlier, the deceased sustained serious injuries and had to undergo multiple surgeries.
PW2 - the doctor has stated that, in such a situation, myocardial infarction can definitely occur.
In such a situation, this Court is of the opinion that, the death of the deceased is attributable to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Resultantly, the findings of the Tribunal in paragraph 10 of the award to the contrary are set aside.
Now, the remaining question that arises for consideration is as regards the various claims made by the appellants herein before the Tribunal.

A claim of Rs.50,000/- was made as against the funeral expenses and the same was totally disallowed on account of the finding to the effect that, the death was not on account of the injuries sustained in the accident.
Similarly, an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- is claimed towards loss of estate, and that is also rejected for the afore reason.

Since this Court has already found that the death is attributable to the injuries sustained in the accident,
the above findings of the Tribunal are not correct.
However, this Court is of the opinion that the entire claim made is not to be accepted, and a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate can be awarded.

Similarly, an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- was also claimed towards loss of love and affection, which has been rejected on account of the finding that the death has no connection with the injuries sustained in the accident.
In view of the reversal of the above conclusion by the Tribunal, the appellants-petitioners would be entitled to receive an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection.
As MACA No.4153 of 2019 2024:KER:73502 regards the loss of dependency claimed at Rs.10,00,000/-, this Court notices that, the deceased was aged 78.
However, age may not be a criteria while deciding claims as regards the loss of dependency.
Similarly, the financial dependency of the claimants is also not a relevant criteria.
[See Thomas George v. Santha [2016 (4) KHC 237].

Therefore, the appellants are entitled to the claim as regards the loss of dependency and the same is to be calculated with reference to the monthly income of the deceased estimated by the Tribunal at Rs.5,000/- as under, after reducing 1/3rd towards personal/living expenses.
In such circumstances, the claim is limited to Rs.2,00,000/-.
The findings of the Tribunal with respect to the balance claims appear to be correct.
